html:
SMTO-EML-0001 — SMTO couldn't get your email ready to send

GUID: 319d6035-156d-5896-b433-d5415fe8fe00
Slug: email-profile-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while preparing your email because something in the message or its saved sender settings didn't pass its checks. This older message doesn't say which part, and it can't confirm whether anything was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and look for the part SMTO names, such as the sender profile, a recipient list, the subject or the message text. This older error code does not establish which part failed, but the details often name it.
  2. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu (the ⋯ button at the top), select the email sender profile you used, and make sure it still exists and its server, port and sender address are filled in. SMTO reads the sender settings fresh for every email and stops if the profile is missing or incomplete.
  3. Before asking SMTO to send again, check the sender mailbox's Sent folder (if your provider keeps one), or ask a recipient, whether the email arrived. This error alone doesn't prove the email wasn't sent, so checking first avoids sending a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the mail server accepted the message, and it reaches your recipients only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's email settings. Don't change your email password or reconnect the account just because of this message; it doesn't mean your sign-in was refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Email preparation failed validation under the legacy email_profile_invalid or email_profile_not_found identity, which by itself does not identify the failed field or preparation stage.

What this means

  • Older producers used this identity for message, sender profile, revision and local preparation failures. Without a retained precise identity or field, the specific cause remains unknown. Inspection-only connected:false does not establish rejected credentials.

Why this can happen

  • A legacy EmailError default was emitted without a precise message, profile or dependency reference.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect any retained field and phase. If they are absent, keep the cause unknown rather than deriving it from transcript prose.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the retained field, failure_phase and error_ref in Technical details or the email tool result, then correct only that input: the email_smtp sender profile in Parameter Store (validate_profile), the to/cc/bcc/subject/body arguments, or tls.ca_pem. Check status, executed and effect_unknown before any resend, and do not reconnect OAuth or rotate credentials on the basis of this code alone.
  • Read the retained field, preparation stage and result details. Correct only the problem established there; do not reconnect an account or change credentials solely because of this legacy code.

Retry and execution caution

  • The legacy identity alone establishes neither nonexecution nor a safe retry; use the retained execution and delivery evidence.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact message and current sender profile validate together before sending.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
